label: Kesong puti
note: The vinegar version is not fermented and is slightly sour, the rennet version is firmer. Salted in the milk or in brine afterwards, sold wrapped in banana leaf

about.text: A soft, unaged white cheese from the Philippines, made from unskimmed carabao (water buffalo) milk and salt, set with rennet, vinegar or citrus juice and traditionally sold wrapped in banana leaf.

sources.text: The first paragraph of its article, shortened.
The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.text: Traditionally vinegar sets it, which makes it slightly sour and soft; the Philippine Carabao Center teaches rennet instead, for a firmer, milder cheese.

steps.note: Left undisturbed with calf or carabao rennet (PCC/Laguna), or with vinegar or citrus juice (Bulacan, Cavite).
In 1–2 in cubes, rested 10 min, then cut smaller and rested 15 min.
400 g salt in 5 L boiled, cooled (35–40 °C) water is added to the cut curd for 20 min, or 1–4 tsp salt in the milk at home.
